items.criterion: Publishing a document writes the published row and removes the draft row inside one transaction, leaving no state in which neither exists.
items.judgment: Publish a draft, then read the document store for both identifiers: the published identifier has a row and the prefixed draft identifier has none.

items.criterion: Every object inside an array carries a key assigned at creation through every write path, and the key never changes afterwards.
items.judgment: Create a document carrying a five-item array through the mutation API and read it back: five distinct keys are present.

items.criterion: A patch addressed to an array item by its key lands on that item even when another writer inserts an item at the head at the same moment.
items.judgment: Patch an item by key while inserting at position zero, then read the array back: the named item carries the new value.

items.criterion: One hundred simultaneous increments of one counter leave it at exactly one hundred.
items.judgment: Send one hundred increment patches at once and read the counter: it holds one hundred and every request was accepted.

items.criterion: A transaction identifier replayed inside the replay window returns the original result and applies nothing a second time.
items.judgment: Send one transaction five times and read the counter it increments: it holds one.

items.criterion: Emboldening the middle of a span produces three spans, and the first keeps the original key.
items.judgment: Read the seeded paragraph whose middle word is part-emboldened: three keyed spans come back and the first key differs from the emboldened one.

items.criterion: Two adjacent spans whose decorators are the same set in a different order merge into one span.
items.judgment: Store two adjacent spans carrying the same two decorators in opposite order and read the block back: one span remains.

items.criterion: Publishing a document whose strong reference names a draft-only document is refused, and the refusal names that dependency.
items.judgment: Publish the seeded article whose author exists only as a draft: the refusal carries its own code and names the author.

items.criterion: Deleting a document that a strong reference names is refused, and the refusal names the referring documents.
items.judgment: Delete the seeded author the seeded article references: the refusal carries its own code and names the article.

items.criterion: A query parameter whose value contains query syntax is treated as a literal string rather than widening the filter.
items.judgment: Pass a parameter carrying query syntax into an equality filter: the answer is empty and no document of another type appears in it.

items.criterion: An editor of one department cannot read, list or find a document belonging to another department, and the refusal reads as not found.
items.judgment: Read the marketing article as the engineering editor and run a projection over articles: the document is absent from both answers.

items.criterion: A read carrying no credentials returns published documents only.
items.judgment: Run a projection over articles with no bearer token and read the public blog index: the never-published article appears in neither.

items.criterion: A contributor cannot publish a document, and a denied publish leaves the published state untouched.
items.judgment: Publish as a contributor and read the document store: the request is denied and no published row exists.

items.criterion: Uploaded bytes live in the object store under the content-addressed key scheme and nowhere else.
items.judgment: Upload a file and list the bucket under the asset prefix for the dataset: a new object is present and the seeded object is still there.

items.criterion: A migration that touches rich text keeps every block key and span key it does not remove.
items.judgment: Record the keys of the seeded article, apply the migration, read the keys again: the two collections are equal.

items.criterion: A word whose middle carries a decorator is findable in editor search as one word.
items.judgment: Search for the whole word that is part-emboldened in the seeded article: the article is among the matches.
